rationale: Gut-bone review describes kefir as fermented food containing microbial products; no isolated Parkinson outcome.
Infant probiotic trial lists egg sensitivity as an adverse-event category; it does not test a poached-egg intervention.
The narrative review discusses grape-derived polyphenols and grape-rich feeding in nonclinical metabolic models. No dietary whole-grape result for the assigned Parkinson outcome is isolated.
Coffee abstention is part of the autonomic assessment protocol in Wilson disease. The study supplies no coffee treatment comparison.
Anti-aging review names olive-oil-derived hydroxytyrosol in mechanistic context, not isolated culinary PD treatment.
Oligosaccharide review cites fish and shrimp farming applications, not shrimp consumption or a Parkinson outcome.
Historical pharmacopoeia review identifies saffron in an aloe-myrrh-lemon mixed pill, with no measured Parkinson depression outcome.
